- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; apply downward bias of 2–4% for 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 82, true price often drops; adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after day 5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model misinterprets momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for smoothing.
